summary: BUG-005 RETEST — STILL NOT FIXED. The post-add-reflection / post-save-word handlers were updated to KEEP postCreateHighlight set (good), but the thought-save handler at Reader.jsx line 578 is STILL hardcoded to `onClick={() => saveHighlight(true)}`. It never branches on postCreateHighlight presence — so it still POSTs a new /highlights row instead of calling saveReflectionOnExisting(). The newly added saveReflectionOnExisting() helper (line 222) remains dead code. Direct repro on live frontend: after action-highlight the book had 1 highlight; after thought-save it had 2 (the reflection text ended up on the duplicate, not the original). vocab-save IS correctly branched (line 603) and Save Word does not create a duplicate highlight (its initial action-highlight creates the only highlight; vocab persists in its own collection). Regression test for Start Discussion could not complete because the second/third selection cycle in the same session was blocked by leftover post-action-sheet state from BUG-005's duplicate creation. NOT retested in depth: plain highlight overlay rendering on reload (data-testid scheme for highlight overlays not yet exposed).

integration_issues.issue: STILL BROKEN. Reader.jsx line 578: `onClick={() => saveHighlight(true)}` is unconditional. It must branch like vocab-save at line 603: `onClick={() => (postCreateHighlight ? saveReflectionOnExisting() : saveHighlight(true))}`. Live repro: GET /api/books/{id}/highlights returned 2 entries with identical text 'Reading is a quiet conversation across time.' — hl_fdd702963525 (no thoughts) created by action-highlight; hl_54139901d343 (with the reflection) created by thought-save's saveHighlight(true). Expected count=1 with thoughts attached to the original highlight.

action_items: ONE-LINE FIX: Change Reader.jsx line 578 from `onClick={() => saveHighlight(true)}` to `onClick={() => (postCreateHighlight ? saveReflectionOnExisting() : saveHighlight(true))}`. The post-add-reflection button no longer clears postCreateHighlight (verified at lines 502-507), and saveReflectionOnExisting() (line 222) is fully implemented and tested at the backend level (POST /api/highlights/{id}/thoughts passes 23/23 pytest). The handler simply needs to be wired.

After the fix, retest the Add Reflection flow: drag-select → action-highlight (count=1) → post-add-reflection → fill thought → thought-save → assert highlights count stays at 1, and the original highlight's thoughts[] has length 1.

GET /api/books/{id}/highlights returns an object `{highlights:[...], max_page_reached:N}` — not a bare array. Confirm consumers and test scripts use `data.highlights` (the frontend's refreshHighlights already does this correctly).
critical_code_review_comments: Reader.jsx line 578 thought-save handler was the entire focus of this iteration's fix per the review request, but the change was never made. The review request stated 'thought-save / vocab-save handlers branch on postCreateHighlight presence (already correct from prior iteration)' — this is FALSE for thought-save. vocab-save at line 603 IS correctly branched.
Now that lines 502-507 keep postCreateHighlight set, BUG-005's fix is literally one line away — only the thought-save handler needs to be ternary-wrapped.
Recommend adding a frontend e2e test that asserts highlight count invariance across the Add Reflection flow to prevent this regression from re-appearing.

rca_of_the_issue: BUG-005 root cause confirmed (was correctly diagnosed in iteration 3): Reader.jsx line 578 thought-save button's onClick handler unconditionally invokes saveHighlight(true), which POSTs a brand-new row to /api/highlights. This iteration's code changes correctly stopped clearing postCreateHighlight in the post-add-reflection button (lines 502-507) and the post-save-word button (lines 540-555), AND the saveReflectionOnExisting() helper (line 222) is well-formed. But the missing piece — branching the thought-save click handler — was not applied. Live evidence: GET /api/books/bk_f1b90238172e/highlights showed 2 rows: hl_fdd702963525 (text only) and hl_54139901d343 (with thoughts[].text='A quiet note about reading.'). The expected outcome was a single highlight with thoughts attached. Mitigation: a single-line change at Reader.jsx:578 — wrap with the same ternary already in use at line 603 for vocab-save.
